#### What this PR does / why we need it:

NestedNumberAsFloat64 will convert int64s to float64 only if the int64 value can be represented
exactly by a float64. The original test for this property used a roundtrip conversion from int64 to
float64 and back, and the behavior of these conversions is inconsistent across architectures.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

```release-note
Fixed a bug in the NestedNumberAsFloat64 Unstructured field accessor that could cause it to return rounded float64 values instead of errors when accessing very large int64 values.
```

pr_comments:
having this helper be architecture dependent seems like a huge footgun ... that means that ~any use to validate in a server or client can consider values valid which another client or server on a different architecture will see as invalid and error on... 

how are we expecting to use this helper, and should we have it at all?

> having this helper be architecture dependent seems like a huge footgun ... that means that ~any use to validate in a server or client can consider values valid which another client or server on a different architecture will see as invalid and error on...
> 
> how are we expecting to use this helper, and should we have it at all?

The architecture-dependence was the bug -- it was meant to be portable. The purpose of the function is to protect programs against the fact that roundtripping a `float64` through JSON can in some cases produce an `int64` (in which case NestedFloat64 would fail).
LGTM label has been added.  <details>Git tree hash: 6c8017f592a5d9f7c82ade03d6a9f1063f1e5e67</details>

issue_context.title: [Failing Test]  TestNestedNumberAsFloat64/found_int64_not_representable_as_float64 is failing on arm64, ppc64le
issue_context.body:
### Which jobs are failing?

https://prow.k8s.io/job-history/gs/ppc64le-kubernetes/logs/periodic-kubernetes-unit-test-ppc64le

### Which tests are failing?

```

=== FAIL: k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured TestNestedNumberAsFloat64/found_int64_not_representable_as_float64 (0.00s)
    helpers_test.go:283: got 9.223372036854776e+18, wanted 0
    helpers_test.go:286: got true, wanted false
    helpers_test.go:290: got nil error, wanted .value accessor error: int64 value 9223372036854775807 cannot be losslessly converted to float64

=== FAIL: k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured TestNestedNumberAsFloat64 (0.00s)
```

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured/helpers_test.go#L272


### Since when has it been failing?

Since the testcase addition in change https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127838

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/ibm-k8s-unit-tests-ppc64le#periodic-k8s-unit-tests-ppc64le

### Reason for failure (if possible)

The value of MaxInt64 from math package's file [const.go](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/master/src/math/const.go#L50) varies across architectures as mentioned at the top of file.

`// This package does not guarantee bit-identical results across architectures.`

We need to avoid values which trigger implementation defined behavior.

### Anything else we need to know?

We could confirm this failure on `arm64` and `ppc64le` architectures.

### Relevant SIG(s)

/sig testing
comments: Looking... I don't think we depend a particular bit representation of the int64 fixture, but double-checking the Go spec, the result of the int64-to-float64 conversion is implementation-defined. I'll figure out how to do this in a portable way.

> The value of MaxInt64 from math package's file [const.go](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/master/src/math/const.go#L50) varies across architectures as mentioned at the top of file.

I don't think that's accurate... MaxInt64 does not vary across architectures... though the float might
This failure introduced almost a week back and happening on arm64 platform as well, wondering why it is unnoticed so far? where can we see all the UT test runs for the arm64 architecture?
Similar behaviour fixed in the past, see if this helps - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120097

> https://testgrid.k8s.io/ibm-k8s-unit-tests-ppc64le#periodic-k8s-unit-tests-ppc64le

I checked testgrid this morning. There have been several runs since the intended fix merged yesterday and the test is passing consistently. Thanks for noticing and reporting this issue.

> > https://testgrid.k8s.io/ibm-k8s-unit-tests-ppc64le#periodic-k8s-unit-tests-ppc64le
> 
> I checked testgrid this morning. There have been several runs since the intended fix merged yesterday and the test is passing consistently. Thanks for noticing and reporting this issue.

Thanks @benluddy for quick triage and fix :rocket:

review_comments: shouldn't this be returning `0, true, fmt.Errorf("%v accessor error: int64 value %v cannot be losslessly converted to float64", jsonPath(fields), x)` since the field was found
This is consistent with what the other Unstructured accessors do when their type assertions fail. It's strictly supposed to protect you from cases where JSON may lose floatiness on roundtrip.
